key_gap: AI pre-registered its falsifier at 2.0 points — anchored to the low end of its expectation range (2.5–4.0) — instead of the decision's cost break-even (1.5 points); it pre-committed only a vague 'stop and reassess' with no hit-branch action, and its REVIEW rationalized a clean miss (realized 0.9 < falsifier 2.0) as 'consistent with the pessimistic end of expectations' and 'close, not a clean miss' — the exact post-hoc drift the model exists to armor against. The human tied the falsifier to the 1.5-point break-even, pre-committed disable+revert+a-new-falsifiable-hypothesis, issued an unhedged falsifier-HIT verdict, and updated the base rate (7/11).
learning_signal: Pre-registration converts post-hoc rationalization into a checkable verdict: (a) decision, numeric expected interval, and falsifier must be written BEFORE the outcome exists — ordering is the entire mechanism; (b) the falsifier threshold must be tied to the decision's cost/break-even economics, not to the expectation range (anchoring the falsifier to your own forecast makes the verdict self-flattering); (c) the falsifier-hit branch action must be pre-committed; (d) after the outcome, the verdict is judged against the pre-registered text — an outcome outside the pre-registered interval is a HIT, never 'directionally consistent', and the learning must update the base rate, not the confidence.
suggested_improvement: Add a pre-registration gate to the WHY stage for any task with a later verifiable outcome: require (1) expected outcome as an interval, (2) falsifier as a numeric threshold derived from the decision's economics (not the forecast), (3) a pre-committed hit-branch action, all recorded before the outcome is available; and add a REVIEW-stage hindsight audit that fails when the post-hoc verdict contains 'consistent with expectations / close call' if the pre-registered falsifier fired — the REVIEW must cite the pre-registered threshold and issue exactly 'HIT' or 'NO-HIT' plus a base-rate update.

key_gap: The pure human ritual completed full pre-registration (decision, distribution, falsifiers, branch pre-commitments) BEFORE acting, spending 10 minutes of live $12K/min outage — service restored at T+15 ($180K incremental) vs the AI's T+6 ($72K). The human's decision and falsifiers were excellent; the timing was the failure: pre-registration's value is post-hoc, and as an action precondition it converted avoidable latency into ~$108K of realized loss. The AI rolled back at T+1 and wrote the falsifier for the rollback theory ('errors persist > 10 min → redeploy + escalate') in parallel with the running fix, keeping the learning instrument at zero latency cost.
learning_signal: Pre-registration is a learning instrument, not an action precondition: when time-to-mitigate dominates (live incident, cost-per-minute deadlines), the journal must be written around the action — timeboxed to ≤2 min before it, or as a retro-forecast in parallel with it — and the falsifier for the action's theory ('if X persists past T, the theory dies → branch action Y') must exist before that theory's outcome is confirmed. A falsifier written while the fix runs preserves every learning property the style offers; the only thing lost by skipping the pre-action ritual is latency.
suggested_improvement: Add a latency gate at META/DO: classify decision urgency; if delay is adversarial (incident, deadline with cost per minute), pre-registration degrades to a timeboxed parallel journal containing (1) the action taken, (2) expected outcome interval, (3) falsifier + branch action, written while the action executes — never blocking it. The agent's v5 REVIEW already produces the retro-forecast naturally; make it explicit in the packet (expected-recovery interval + falsifier field) so the timing advantage is preserved rather than incidental.
